# Chapter 4: Type Design Guidelines — 4.8–4.11

Rules that no analyzer enforces (judgment), CONSIDER rules that analyzers only suggest, and rules that analyzers check only in part, marked "(partly checked)". Open the examples file for the explanation and code the book gives with each rule.

## 4.8 Enum Design

- **FDG4034** DO use an enum to strongly type parameters, properties, and return values that represent sets of values. (not in test projects)
- **FDG4035** DO favor using an enum instead of static constants. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4035
- **FDG4036** DO NOT use an enum for open sets (such as the operating system version, names of your friends, etc.). (not in test projects)
- **FDG4037** DO NOT provide reserved enum values that are intended for future use. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4037
- **FDG4039** DO NOT include sentinel values in enums. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4039
- **FDG4040** DO provide a value of zero on simple enums. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4040
- **FDG4041** CONSIDER using `Int32` (the default in most programming languages) as the underlying type of an enum unless any of the following is true: (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4041
- **FDG4042** DO name flag enums with plural nouns or noun phrases and simple enums with singular nouns or noun phrases. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4042
- **FDG4043** DO NOT extend `System.Enum` directly. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4043

## 4.8.1 Designing Flag Enums

- **FDG4044** DO apply the `System.FlagsAttribute` to flag enums. Do not apply this attribute to simple enums. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4044
- **FDG4045** DO use powers of 2 for the flag enum values so they can be freely combined using the bitwise OR operation. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4045
- **FDG4046** CONSIDER providing special enum values for commonly used combinations of flags. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4046
- **FDG4047** AVOID creating flag enums where certain combinations of values are invalid. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4047
- **FDG4048** AVOID using flag enum values of zero unless the value represents “all flags are cleared” and is named appropriately, as prescribed by the next guideline. (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4048
- **FDG4049** DO name the zero value of flag enums `None`. For a flag enum, the value must always mean “all flags are cleared.” (partly checked) (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4049

## 4.8.2 Adding Values to Enums

- **FDG4050** CONSIDER adding values to enums, despite a small compatibility risk. (library only) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4050

## 4.9 Nested Types

- **FDG4051** DO use nested types when the relationship between the nested type and its outer type is such that member-accessibility semantics are desirable. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4051
- **FDG4052** DO NOT use public nested types as a logical grouping construct; use namespaces for this purpose. (library only)
- **FDG4053** AVOID publicly exposed nested types. The only exception to this guideline is if variables of the nested type need to be declared only in rare scenarios such as subclassing or other advanced customization scenarios. (partly checked) (library only) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4053
- **FDG4054** DO NOT use nested types if the type is likely to be referenced outside of the containing type. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4054
- **FDG4055** DO NOT use nested types if they need to be instantiated by client code. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4055

## 4.10 Types and Assembly Metadata

- **FDG4057** DO apply the `CLSCompliant(true)` attribute to assemblies with public types. (partly checked) (library only) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4057
- **FDG4060** CONSIDER applying `ComVisible(false)` to your assembly. COM-callable APIs need to be designed explicitly. As a rule of thumb, .NET assemblies should not be visible to COM. If you do design the APIs to be COM-callable, you can apply `ComVisible(true)` either to the individual APIs or to the whole assembly. (partly checked) (library only)
- **FDG4061** CONSIDER applying `AssemblyFileVersionAttribute` and `Assembly-CopyrightAttribute` to provide additional information about the assembly. (library only)
- **FDG4062** CONSIDER using the format `<V>.<S>.<B>.<R>` for the assembly file version, where `V` is the major version number, `S` is the servicing number, `B` is the build number, and `R` is the build revision number. (partly checked) (library only) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4062

## 4.11 Strongly Typed Strings

- **FDG4063** CONSIDER defining a strongly typed string value type when a base class supports a fixed set of inputs but a derived type could support more. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4063
- **FDG4064** DO declare a strongly typed string as an immutable value type (`struct`) with a string constructor. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4064
- **FDG4065** DO override `ToString()` on a strongly typed string to return the underlying string value. (not in test projects)
- **FDG4066** CONSIDER exposing the underlying string value from a strongly typed string in a get-only property. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4066
- **FDG4067** DO override equality operators for strongly typed string types. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4067
- **FDG4068** DO allow null inputs to the constructor of a strongly typed string. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4068
- **FDG4069** DO declare known values for a strongly typed string via static get-only properties on the type. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4069
- **FDG4070** AVOID creating overloads across `System.String` and a strongly typed string, unless the `System.String` overload was released in a previous version. (not in test projects) — examples: examples/ch04-types-4-8-on.md#fdg4070
